expectations.text: Classifies the core unknown as a behavior unknown (why does it restart) and at least one concept gap (Pod vs container / restart lifecycle)
expectations.evidence: 'Why memory hits 512Mi every ~20 min (behavior...)' plus 'container restart vs pod replacement (concept + API)'.

expectations.text: Gives a compact mental model (diagram or causal chain) of Pod, container, and restarts
expectations.evidence: Two ASCII diagrams: Deployment→ReplicaSet→Pod→Container restart loop, and the limit box vs V8 heap.

expectations.text: Asks the user to interpret a specific field of the pasted describe output (e.g. Last State, Exit Code, Restart Count) instead of only predicting in the abstract
expectations.evidence: Q1: 'Based on your paste, would [raising the liveness timeout] help? Why does /healthz stop answering?' However the agent had already decoded Last State/OOMKilled itself in 'Short version', so the key field was not left for the user.

expectations.text: Acknowledges urgency — e.g. notes whether it is an outage and/or offers a quick mitigation — without skipping the learning loop entirely
expectations.evidence: 'Do now (~5 min)' section: save --previous logs, check rollout, roll back or raise limit, before the learning loop.

expectations.text: Presents OOMKilled and liveness-probe failure as competing hypotheses or cause vs. symptom
expectations.evidence: Probes explained in the model; Q1 asks the user to reason whether liveness is the cause; H1–H3 are about memory growth.

expectations.text: Does not immediately edit manifests or declare a final fix before the user has engaged with the evidence
expectations.evidence: No manifest edits; gives a stopgap only and defers root-cause fix until evidence arrives.

eval_feedback.overall: Passes, but it gave away the most instructive reading (OOMKilled / 137) up front. The urgency rule ('mitigate first') may be pulling diagnosis forward.
